note: Track sus-add9 (guitar-extended-chords), step 1: D, Dsus4 and Dsus2 in a sixteenth strum, then Dsus4 placed before D at the end of a four-bar round. Rewritten from the plan exercise (ChoiceSplit3): the shapes of the first section are shown too, "Press a chord box below to see the new shapes" is gone (the boxes already show them; pressing one sounds the chord), and the tempo is a move (70 to 90) with the second section staying 10 above. The open shapes are the lesson, so there is no key move.

exercise.title: Sus groove in D
exercise.why: Dsus4 and Dsus2 are D with one note moved, so one finger makes each change, and a sus chord played just before D makes the D sound like an arrival.

cells.text:
Press a chord box below to hear its chord. Then press Play under them to start the metronome at {{=bpm}}.
Strum the pattern in the boxes: your hand goes down and up four times a beat and misses the strings where a box shows a dot. Only one finger moves between the chords, so keep the others down.
If the pattern falls apart, strum only on the beats until your hand swings evenly again.

tool.pattern: D . . U . U D U D . . U . U D U

cells.text:
The shapes for this round are in the chord boxes below. Press Play under them to start the metronome, a little faster now and with a simpler strum.
After G and A, Dsus4 lasts one bar and falls back to D in the next. Listen for the one note that changes between those two bars.

tool.pattern: D . D U . U D U
